stops.name: Zagreb, the birth of the medium
stops.campa: On the last night of October a girl is born in Zagreb to a Croat father and a mother of Vienna, and the tradition marks her from the first as a child of striking beauty. She grows with hair the colour of pale wheat, worn long and unbound against the fashion, for in the mythos this hair is no vanity but an antenna, a filament tuned to voices no one else can hear. Already, the circle will later say, the great star of Taurus leans toward the cradle. She is Maria Orsitsch, and the century that will vanish her has only just begun.

stops.name: Vienna, the Schopenhauer café, the first meeting
stops.campa: In wartime Vienna, at a table in the Café Schopenhauer, the young medium from Zagreb is drawn into a company of seekers: the geopolitician Karl Haushofer, the occultist Rudolf von Sebottendorff, the flyer Lothar Waiz, a bishop named Gernot. They have read the Golden Dawn and pondered the secret orders of the East, and they listen when Maria speaks of the voices in her hand. Here, the tradition holds, the thread is first knotted that will run to Munich, to Aldebaran, and to the machines. She leaves the café marked as one of them.

stops.name: Knebworth, the word Vril, from Bulwer-Lytton's coming race
stops.campa: Half a century before Munich, an English lord and novelist gives the coming circle its holy word. Edward Bulwer-Lytton publishes 'The Coming Race': deep beneath the earth dwells the Vril-ya, a superior subterranean people who wield an all-purpose force called Vril: the power of flight, healing and annihilation, the mastery of nature by will. He means it, he tells a friend, for electricity dimly guessed. But the theosophists take it for occult truth; Blavatsky weaves Vril into a doctrine of race. So the word waits, charged, for the women who will claim it as their own.
stops.quote: There is no word in any language I know which is an exact synonym for vril. I should call it electricity, except that it comprehends in its manifold branches other forces of nature.
stops.quote_source: Edward Bulwer-Lytton, 'The Coming Race' (Vril: The Power of the Coming Race), 1871

stops.name: Munich, arrival, and the Thule adjacency
stops.campa: In 1919 Maria comes to Munich with her betrothed and steps at once into the orbit of the Thule Gesellschaft, that lodge of runes and Germanic myth. But she will not be a guest in another's order. The city is raw with revolution and defeat, and in its cafés and back rooms she begins to gather her own: young women mediums who wear their hair long in braids and ponytails when the age has cut its hair short, believing, as she does, that the uncut strand is a receiver for the beyond. Munich becomes the cradle of the circle.

stops.name: Munich, the founding of the Vril Gesellschaft
stops.campa: Maria and her friend Traute name their order in plain German cover: the Alldeutsche Gesellschaft für Metaphysik, the All-German Society for Metaphysics. To the initiated it is the Vril Gesellschaft, and its women take the old power-word of Bulwer-Lytton's coming race: Vril, the force that runs beneath the earth. It is a society almost wholly of women, a chieftaincy of mediums: Maria first, then Sigrun, then Traute, and after them the names Gudrun and Heike. They wear their braids like cables strung to heaven and wait for the message they are certain is coming.

stops.name: Berchtesgaden, the forester's lodge, the first transmission
stops.campa: In December, in a forester's lodge in the wooded hills near Berchtesgaden, Maria and Sigrun sit in trance and Maria's hand begins to move without her will. Two stacks of writing come out of her: one in a script no one present can read, later named a secret German Templar cipher; the other in an old eastern tongue that scholars of the circle call ancient Sumerian. When it is deciphered, it is not prophecy but engineering: technical instructions for the building of a flying machine. The message, the circle declares, comes from Aldebaran.

stops.name: Aldebaran, the star and the empire Sumeran
stops.campa: The decipherers read what the star has sent. Around the sun of Aldebaran, sixty-eight light-years off in Taurus, turn two inhabited worlds that form the empire called Sumeran. Its people are divided into a master race of light-god beings, the Aryans, and lesser human kinds descended from them by decline. When their own sun began to swell, these light-god people rode the void and settled Mars, then Mallona, then Earth, seeding at Sumer the first civilization. So the circle's cosmology holds: the German is the far child of Aldebaran, and the voice in Maria's hand is the voice of home.
stops.quote: The solar system Aldebaran has a sun around which revolve two inhabited planets that form the empire 'SUMERAN'. The population is divided into the master race of 'light God people' (Aryans) and several other human races.
stops.quote_source: Vril transmission text as given in the postwar tradition (Living Moon / Ratthofer lineage)

stops.name: Munich, the séance at Rudolf Hess's apartment
stops.campa: In the late November of 1924, in Rudolf Hess's Munich rooms, Maria sits with Sebottendorff to call the dead Thule poet Dietrich Eckart across the veil. The trance takes her hard; her eyes roll white in her head; and through her a voice announces itself: 'Sumi, the inhabitants of a distant world orbiting the star Aldebaran.' It is no longer a script on paper but a mouth. The beings of the Vril-ya speak into the room, and the circle understands that the channel to the star is open and will not close.
stops.quote: Sumi, the inhabitants of a distant world orbiting the star Aldebaran.
stops.quote_source: Vril séance account (Living Moon / esoteric-center tradition)

stops.name: Munich, the drawing of the Jenseitsflugmaschine
stops.campa: From the Aldebaran sheets the circle draws a machine that has never been flown: the Jenseitsflugmaschine, the Beyond-Flight-Machine, a disc that will rise not on wings but on a force the transmissions name. In Munich, under Professor W. O. Schumann of the Technical University, the first disc is built: some eight metres across, a drive at its centre driving downward against the world. It is not a weapon and not, they insist, a mere aeroplane; it is a craft meant one day to answer the star that called.

stops.name: Augsburg, the machine dismantled and stored
stops.campa: After two years of tethered trials the Beyond-Machine is stopped and taken apart. The pieces are carried to Messerschmitt's works at Augsburg and stored against a later hour, and from the research Schumann keeps a levitation unit the circle will call the SM-Levitator. The first disc sleeps in a hangar; but the drawings do not sleep. In the mythos this is only an intermission: the drive is proven, the principle is held, and the war that is coming will wake the whole design.

stops.name: Brandenburg, the RFZ discs at the Arado works
stops.campa: On the grounds of the Arado aircraft works at Brandenburg the design wakes as the RFZ 1, the first Rundflugzeug. On its single flight, the tradition says, it climbs straight up to some sixty metres, then hangs wobbling and dancing in the air for minutes before it is wrestled down. By year's end the RFZ 2 follows, steadier, steered by a magnetic-impulse field and driven by the Vril force. The discs of the beyond have left the séance room and entered the hangar of the state.

stops.name: The Vril-1 Jäger takes the air
stops.campa: As the war widens, the circle's craft takes fighting form. The Vril-1 Jäger, the Hunter, lifts off: a single-seat disc some eleven and a half metres across, its Vril drive humming beneath one pilot. It is the fruit of two decades of transmission and trial, the séance made metal. In the mythos it is the first true ship of the beyond to fly for the Reich, and behind it in the drawings wait its heavier kin, discs of far greater span already promised by the sheets from Aldebaran.
